elements.label: Open navigation menu and submenu (UI card) scaling up toward the top-left

elements.manual_reason: No candidate box isolates the cursor; it travels from the Workday logo down onto the Assumptions row.
elements.label: Mouse cursor moving onto Assumptions

pattern.description: Following the cut to the opened navigation menu, the UI scales up about 27% anchored toward the top-left so the menu and Integration submenu fill the frame, settling with a fast-start, long-tail decel; the cursor then lands on a menu row and it highlights.
pattern.why_premium: The zoom makes small screen-recording text legible and focuses attention on the navigation path being narrated, and the strong ease-out makes the move feel deliberate rather than mechanical.

build_hint.gsap: gsap.fromTo(uiCard, {scale: 1}, {scale: 1.27, x: '+=4%', y: '+=3%', transformOrigin: '10% 10%', duration: 0.4, ease: 'expo.out'}); then cursor gsap.to(cursor, {x, y, duration: 0.3, ease: 'power2.out'}) and set the row highlight on arrival.
build_hint.remotion: const p = spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 30, stiffness: 120, mass: 1}}); scale = interpolate(p, [0, 1], [1, 1.27]) with transformOrigin near the top-left (no overshoot); or interpolate over ~12 frames with Easing.out(Easing.exp).

notes: Worth a human look: camera.move is 'none' but scale is 1.27 and the background curve also grows, so this may in fact be a whole-frame push-in that the camera detector missed (large flat dark area on the right). Annotated as the UI card scaling, with pattern ui_camera_push_in as the nearest canonical match. Cursor box is manual.
